title: Patch: a play or attack half-built when your turn ends is dropped, not shown again next turn
thread:
**Issue #2924 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2924: Patch: a play or attack half-built when your turn ends is dropped, not shown again next turn
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Online, the turn clock can end your turn while you are halfway through a play or an attack: you have picked an attacker, or a spell's target picker is open. Today that half-built choice is never cleared. The spell's picker stays on screen through the opponent's whole turn. When your next turn starts, the old attacker shows as selected with last turn's targets glowing, and clicking one sends an attack the server refuses.

Once this is built, the board drops a half-built play or attack whenever the turn changes, as it already does when you press Escape.

## Why

- `Game` holds the selection in `interaction` (`apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx:223`). It goes back to `IDLE` only on:
  - a dispatched action (line 512);
  - the result of a click (537);
  - the picker's Cancel (790);
  - the drag layer's cancels (`apps/web/src/game/drag/DragLayer.tsx:352`, `:366`).
- Nothing resets it when the view's turn or active seat changes.
- `highlightFor` (`apps/web/src/game/actions.ts:695-707`) hides a selection only while `legal` is empty or offers nothing but concede. When the next turn's `legal` arrives, the old selection lights up again.
- An attack is then built from `interaction.candidates`, which were captured last turn (`actions.ts:951-958`).
- The play's own picker renders from `outstandingNeed(interaction)` without looking at `legal` (`apps/web/src/game/Prompt.tsx:1900-1903`), so it stays open through the opponent's turn.
- The server ends turns on its own clock: R79's 75-second turn clock and its `timeout`, which ends the active player's turn. So this can happen in any online 1v1 or Duos game where the clock runs out mid-choice.

## Proposal

In `Game`, drop the selection when the shown view's turn, active seat or viewer changes. Use the adjust-state-while-rendering pattern the concede dialog already uses (`Game.tsx:564`): remember the turn the selection was made on, and `setInteraction(IDLE)` when it differs.

Nothing in `actions.ts` or the engine changes. The board still renders only what `legal` lists (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx`.
- `apps/web/src/game/Game.test.tsx`.
- SPEC §10.10 (client rendering). No ruling: no rule changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `Game` test selects an attacker on the player's turn, rerenders with the opponent active and `legal` empty, then rerenders with the player's next turn and its legal moves. No card is selected and no old target glows. This fails today.
- [ ] A play whose own picker is open when the view moves to the opponent's turn: the picker is gone.
- [ ] A selection survives a view update within the same turn (an emote arriving, the opponent's trap prompt resolving). Today's tests stay green.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Game.test.tsx` passes.

## Size and risks

Small: about ten lines and two or three tests. The risk is resetting too eagerly within a turn. Keying on the turn number and the active seat, not on every new view, avoids that.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41648417037)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

When the shown view's turn, active seat, or viewer changes, `Game` drops a half-built play or attack back to `IDLE`, as it already does on Escape. A selected attacker no longer re-lights with last turn's targets on the player's next turn, and a play's own picker no longer stays open through the opponent's turn. A selection survives view updates within the same turn.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx` | change | One `selectionKey` state next to `interaction` (~line 223); one adjust-state-while-rendering reset block after the emote-menu block (~line 571) |
| `apps/web/src/game/Game.test.tsx` | change | Three tests in a new `describe`; extend the fixtures import with `card` and `waitingPending` |

Do not touch: `crates/*`, `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`, `apps/web/src/game/Prompt.tsx`, `apps/web/src/game/drag/DragLayer.tsx`, `spec/*`, or anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`. Governing spec section is §10.10 (client renders `viewFor` and decides nothing, CLAUDE.md rule 7). No ruling: no rule changes, so no note under `spec/rulings/`, no `spec/pending/` entry, and no `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Steps

1. Re-read `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx` lines 220–260 (the `interaction` state and the `shown` view), 505–575 (`legal` gated on `shown === view`, the concede adjust-during-render block at line 564 to copy), and `apps/web/src/game/contract.ts` lines 58–70 (`testid.card`, `testid.handCard`).
2. In `Game`, directly after `const [interaction, setInteraction] = useState<Interaction>(IDLE);` (~line 223), add:
   `const [selectionKey, setSelectionKey] = useState<string | null>(null);`
   with a comment naming the turn clock (§10.10): the key is the shown turn, active seat, and viewer the selection was built on.
3. After the emote-menu adjust-during-render block (~line 571, before the `useEffect` on `shown.result`), add the reset, computing the key from `shown`, never from `view`:
   `const shownKey = `${shown.turn}:${shown.active}:${shown.viewer}`;`
   `if (selectionKey !== shownKey) { setSelectionKey(shownKey); if (interaction.stage !== "idle") setInteraction(IDLE); }`
   Keying on the remembered shown key (not `shown` vs `view`) matters: while an animation holds the board back, `shown` is old and `view` is new, and comparing them would drop the selection mid-animation on every animated turn change. This copies the concede dialog's pattern at line 564, so no effect is needed and nothing flashes for one frame.
4. Do not change `actions.ts`, `Prompt.tsx`, or `DragLayer.tsx`. `highlightFor` and `outstandingNeed` already render only the passed `interaction`; once it is `IDLE` the glow and the play picker vanish on their own.
5. In `Game.test.tsx`, extend the fixtures import (line 15) with `card` and `waitingPending`. Add the three tests from **Tests** below. Build every view with `events: []` (the `baseView` default): with no new events the runner stays idle and `shown` swaps to the new view synchronously, so no timer advances are needed.
6. Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Game.test.tsx` and keep all tests green.

## Tests

All in `apps/web/src/game/Game.test.tsx`, new block `describe("a half-built play or attack is dropped at the turn change (#2924)")`. Shared setup inside the block:

```tsx
const attacker = (): PlayerView => baseView({
  you: emptySide("p1", { units: [unit("p1", { instanceId: "u1" }), null, null, null, null] }),
  opponent: emptySide("p2", { units: [unit("p2", { instanceId: "e1" }), null, null, null, null] }),
});
const attack: ActionBody = { type: "attack", attackerId: "u1", targetId: "e1" };
```

- Test 1, `it("drops the selected attacker when the turn changes and keeps it dropped next turn")`: render `attacker()` with `legal={[attack]}`; `fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId(testid.card("u1")))`; assert `card-u1` has `data-selected="true"` and `[data-testid="card-e1"][data-glow]` is present. Rerender `{ ...attacker(), active: "p2", turn: 4 }` with `legal={[]}`; assert `card-u1` has no `data-selected`. Rerender `{ ...attacker(), turn: 5 }` with `legal={[attack]}`; assert `card-u1` has no `data-selected` and no `[data-glow]` on `card-e1`; then `fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId(testid.card("e1")))` and assert `onAction` was never called. Fails today: the old `interaction.candidates` re-light and the click sends the stale attack.
- Test 2, `it("closes a play's own picker when the view moves to the opponent's turn")`: `mine = baseView({ you: emptySide("p1", { hand: [card({ instanceId: "h1" })] }) })`, `plays = [{ type: "play", instanceId: "h1", zone: { row: "units", lane: 1 } }, { type: "play", instanceId: "h1", zone: { row: "units", lane: 2 } }]`; render `mine` with `legal={plays}`; click `testid.handCard("h1")`; assert `prompt-modal` has `data-prompt-source="play"`. Rerender `{ ...mine, active: "p2", turn: 4 }` with `legal={[]}`; assert `queryByTestId("prompt-scrim")` is null. Fails today: the picker renders from `outstandingNeed(interaction)` regardless of `legal`.
- Test 3, `it("keeps the selected attacker through view updates within the same turn")`: select `u1` as in test 1; rerender `{ ...first, clockMs: 59000 }` with the same legal and assert `card-u1` still has `data-selected="true"`; rerender with `pending: waitingPending` and assert still selected; rerender with `pending: null` and assert still selected.
- Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Game.test.tsx`.

## Done when

- [ ] Selecting an attacker, moving to the opponent's turn, and returning next turn leaves nothing selected, nothing glowing, and a click on the old target sends nothing.
- [ ] A play's own picker open at the turn change is gone on the opponent's turn.
- [ ] A selection survives a same-turn view update (clock tick; opponent's trap prompt appearing and resolving).
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Game.test.tsx` passes with no other test touched.

## Risks

- Resetting too eagerly within a turn (every animated view swap, every `pending` change) would break in-progress plays. Avoided by keying the remembered state on `turn`/`active`/`viewer` only, never on view identity or `events`.
- Game over changes `result` but not turn/active/viewer, so the reset does not fire there; the selection stays in state but invisible via `highlightFor`'s empty-legal path under the result overlay. That matches today; no change needed.
- A pointer drag in flight across the turn change still ends through `DragLayer`'s own cancel path; this change only drops the committed `interaction` state.
- No named constants are added (CLAUDE.md rule 9); the key is a render-local string, not a tunable.

## Open questions

None.
````
